newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters denies NZ heading for spending blowout.
newsitem.headline: Peters denies NZ heading for spending blowout.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters said on Thursday there was no danger of New Zealand government spending slipping in future years.
"Talk of the government expenditure blowing out is nothing but unsubstantiated scaremongering," he said in a statement in response to a critical editorial in the Australian Financial Review.
He said the editorial had peddled what he called "tired assumptions" about New Zealand's economic policy including claims that it would lead to fiscal policy "slippage".
"The editorial is based on claims that have no basis and on the more negative musings of some members of the New Zealand economic analysts' community," he said.
Peters said there would be no pause in the reform process.
The government was not sitting on its hands, he added.
"On numerous occasions ministers have indicated New Zealand can expect a radical shake-up on the welfare state in the budget," he said.

The Austrialian Financial Review's editorial on Wednesday, under the headline "Why New Zealand is no longer First," said the country was in danger of losing the confidence of markets as it went into a period of fiscal expansion.
Dubbing Peters a populist, it said the country's business prospects were dull.
Peters, in turn, cited the electricity industry, the Accident Compensation Corporation and producer boards as areas where reform would continue.
In his statement he said the government would stick to plans to spend more on critical areas of health and eduction.

"The government has been extremely upfront about this, but has emphasised it is not abandoning fiscal responsibility and will keep within its self-imposed spending limit of NZ$5 billion (over three years).".
"We will continue to run healthy surpluses -- unlike the Australian government," he added.
